lesson.title: Axilla, axillary artery and scapular spaces
lesson.summary: The axillary nerve travels with posterior circumflex humeral vessels around the surgical neck.
tags: Axilla, axillary artery and scapular spaces
lesson.section: 18. Axilla and Axillary Artery; 19. Scapular Spaces

steps.title: Axilla and Axillary Artery
steps.body:
The axilla is a pyramidal passage between neck and upper limb. It contains the axillary vessels, cords and branches of the brachial plexus, axillary lymph nodes, and fat.

Apex: cervicoaxillary canal. Base: skin, superficial fascia, axillary fascia. Anterior wall: pectoralis major/minor and clavipectoral fascia. Posterior wall: subscapularis, teres major, latissimus dorsi. Medial wall: serratus anterior and thoracic wall. Lateral wall: humerus, coracobrachialis, short head of biceps.

steps.title: Scapular Spaces
steps.body:
The scapular spaces are high-yield because they test topographic boundaries and neurovascular contents. The quadrangular space transmits the axillary nerve; the triangular interval transmits the radial nerve.

Quadrangular space: teres minor superior, teres major inferior, long head triceps medial, surgical neck lateral. Triangular space: teres minor superior, teres major inferior, long head triceps lateral; contains circumflex scapular artery. Triangular interval: teres major superior, long head triceps medial, humerus/lateral head lateral; contains radial nerve and profunda brachii artery.

steps.title: How does pectoralis minor organize axillary arterial branches?
steps.body: It divides the axillary artery into proximal, posterior and distal parts. The usual pattern assigns one branch to the first part, two to the second and three to the third, including subscapular and circumflex humeral routes distally. Branching varies, so the pattern is a learning framework rather than an invariant count. Trace each branch toward thoracic wall, scapular region or humeral neck. The associated plexus cords use the second arterial part as their naming reference, linking vascular and neural maps.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The axillary nerve travels with posterior circumflex humeral vessels around the surgical neck. The radial nerve and profunda brachii artery use the triangular interval; the circumflex scapular artery uses the triangular space. Similar names can conceal different boundaries and contents. In the axilla, pectoralis minor divides the axillary artery into three parts and helps orient its branches. The brachial plexus cords are named relative to the second part of that artery.
